source.title: Are All Layers Created Equal?
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Y. Singer

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures layer re-initialization and re-randomization effects on test performance, but does not test any listed version: it does not compare natural-label generalization with random-label fitting, test error across widths, compare convolutional and fully connected networks, or measure training–test gaps and magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: Layer reset effects are related to generalization but do not measure a claim version's stated behavior or property. Table 1 reports results for jointly freezing or removing residual blocks; figures report individual-layer effects, with many values available only graphically. The paper also reports adversarial-attack results, which do not bear on the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The main layer-reset experiments test none of the versions. However, the study's unmodified FCN and convolutional baselines on CIFAR-10 bear on V3: Figure 2(b) reports FCN test errors, while Figures 3–4 and Table 3 report substantially lower convolutional-network errors under the study's standard gradient-training setup. This comparison is missing from the extracted rows.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that layers have heterogeneous reset robustness, that individually robust layers need not be jointly robust, and that parameter counts and norms alone are too coarse to explain generalization. They advocate analyses that respect layer structure and architecture.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes post-training layer re-initialization, re-randomization, freezing, and removal, rather than the listed studies' interventions or generalization-gap measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed layer robustness patterns vary with architecture, dataset/task difficulty, model size, training stage used for re-initialization, weight decay, batch normalization, and optimizer in the language-model experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual layers differ in sensitivity to re-initialization and re-randomization, with patterns depending on architecture, capacity, and task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training reset sensitivity is heterogeneous across layers and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing or removing individually robust blocks can worsen performance; the ImageNet removal penalty is larger than the CIFAR-10 penalty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual reset robustness does not guarantee that blocks can be jointly frozen or omitted during training without an accuracy cost.

record.problems: The paper says it does not quantify a universal threshold for negligible performance decline. Many layer-level results are plotted without exact numerical values. The table's layer-reset averages and joint-reset experiments do not directly measure generalization gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only individual-layer and joint-layer results were not extracted as numerical rows because exact values cannot be assigned from the supplied plots. Section 6 Table 2 adversarial attack results were omitted because they do not bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error width threshold under training to convergence; Figure 2 instead emphasizes reset robustness.
Isolating local connectivity, learning sparse local connections, and initializing fully connected networks from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets; using Adam for the language model supplies no such comparison.
Batch-size comparisons within the same workload and fixed epoch budget, including adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.

Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps and rankings against norm and margin measures. Layer resets, parameter distances, and SAM checkpoint comparisons do not establish this relationship.
Removing training examples selected by label memorization and comparing against random example removal.

missing.what: Record the unmodified CIFAR-10 FCN baselines across hidden widths and their comparison with unmodified VGG and ResNet baselines. Exact FCN values are not recoverable from the supplied text rendering; retain the qualitative comparison with that limitation.
missing.locator: Figure 2(b), Section 3.2, Figures 3–4, Table 3, and Appendix A.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted Table 1 values and baselines match the supplied text. Their reset, freezing, and removal contrasts remain unlinked to V1–V8. The incidental unmodified architecture comparison supplies the V3 evidence; neither the paper's general discussion of flatness nor its reproduction of another study's criticality bounds supplies a V7 test.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error across widths relative to the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the stated local-connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus the train–test gap and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: Unmodified FCNs versus VGGs and ResNets trained from scratch on CIFAR-10 with momentum SGD.
relationships.reason: Based on text and figures, with the comparison missing from the rows: Figure 2(b)'s FCN baseline errors are substantially higher than the convolutional baselines in Figures 3–4 and Table 3; Section 3.2 explicitly describes the convolutional advantage. This supports the architecture-level comparison without isolating its cause.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower convolutional baseline errors under momentum SGD remain unverified, and local connectivity was not isolated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
